answers.question: What is the cell phone policy?
answers.content:
Here's the cell phone/smart watch policy that applies across all brands [p.19]:

- Personal cell phones are permitted in the workplace but must be kept out of sight [p.19].
- It's the employee's responsibility to protect the guest experience — texting, phone calls, or social media use while working jeopardizes that [p.9] [p.14] [p.26] [p.31] [p.48].
- Phones should be on silent and not kept on the employee's person (not in back pockets, not charging in the break room, not sitting on top of a drawer till) [p.19].
- The only time a phone should be accessed while clocked in is in an emergency [p.19].
- Smart watches are allowed as long as they aren't used for social media, texting, or calls — and the company can ask an employee to remove one if it starts interfering with the guest experience [p.19].

If you're dealing with a specific situation — like a team member you've seen on their phone repeatedly — happy to help you think through next steps.

answers.question: What is the dress code policy for Buff City Soap and Crunch?
answers.content:
Here's the dress code, pulling the all-locations standards plus each brand's specific rules:

**All Locations — applies to every brand, including Buff City Soap and Crunch**
- Name tags must be worn and visible at all times while working; each employee gets one, with replacements ordered through a manager at the employee's expense [p.15].
- Tennis shoes or other full-coverage closed-toe shoes are required — no sandals, crocs, flip-flops, or other open-toe shoes, and shoes must be tied, clean, and hole-free [p.15].
- Belts must be dark brown or black, and nothing may hang from them (phones, keys, chains, etc.) [p.15].
- Hair of any length/color is fine as long as it's clean, groomed, and out of the face and eyes.
- Facial hair must be clean, well-groomed, and trimmed [p.16].
- Reasonable, natural make-up is acceptable and encouraged [p.16].
- Jewelry is fine if it doesn't interfere with work; no dangling earrings/chains, and no pins or buttons on the shirt unless management approves [p.16].
- Large, inappropriate, or offensive tattoos must be covered; other tattoos are fine if not discriminatory or offensive [p.16].

**Buff City Soap specific**
- Shirts: any plain black, white, or gray t-shirt or long-sleeve shirt may be worn under the branded apron, or any branded top [p.16]. Shirts can't be shorter than the beltline (no exposed stomach) or low-cut, and must be clean and wrinkle-free with no visible patches, rips, or holes [p.16] [p.17].
- Pants: full-length black or blue jean-colored pants are acceptable [p.17]. Yoga pants, joggers, or sweats are never allowed [p.17].

**Crunch Fitness specific**
- Shirts: two uniform shirts provided at hire, with full-time employees getting 1–2 more. Employees may wear a plain black, white, or gray long-sleeve shirt underneath when cold [p.16]. Group Fitness Instructors teaching non-proprietary classes (like Zumba or Pound) may wear fitness-style apparel or class-related branding [p.16]. Shirts can't be shorter than the beltline or low-cut, and must be clean, wrinkle-free, with no visible patches, rips, or holes [p.16] [p.17].
- Pants: yoga pants, joggers, or sweats are approved for Instructors only (preferably solid black) [p.16]. Front Desk and Management must wear solid khaki or black pants, full length, free of holes or fraying [p.16] [p.17].

One general note: the manual states all aspects of dress code are at the Company's discretion — if an employee has a question, check with management before wearing something borderline [p.17].

answers.question: What is the PTO policy?
answers.content:
PTO replaces sick, personal, absence and vacation time as one combined bank. Here's the breakdown:

**Who gets it**
Salaried managers, full-time corporate office personnel, and full-time Assistant Salon Directors/Assistant Makery Managers start accruing PTO after 90 days in that position [p.41]. Temporary or contract employees don't get PTO [p.41].

**Accrual tiers (full-time employees)**
- 90 days–4 years of service: 2 weeks (80 hours), cap of 120 hours [p.41]
- 5–9 years: 3 weeks (120 hours), cap of 160 hours [p.42]
- 10+ years: 4 weeks (160 hours), cap of 200 hours [p.42]

Unused PTO carries over year to year, but once an employee hits the cap for their tier, no more accrues until the balance drops below it [p.42].

**Using it**
- Scheduled in half-day (4 hr) or full-day (8 hr) increments only
- No PTO during each brand's peak season: Sun Tan City Feb 1 and June 1; Buff City Soap Nov 1 and Dec 31; Crunch Jan 1 and Feb 28
- Request it in the Personnel System at least two weeks ahead; for unforeseen situations, call the supervisor directly and enter the request as soon as possible [p.42]
- Needs supervisor approval and won't be granted if it creates undue hardship on the business [p.42]
- Generally only one team member per location/department can be on PTO at the same time, unless the supervisor approves otherwise [p.42]
- Payout on termination follows state and federal guidelines [p.42]

If you meant something more specific — like bereavement leave or FMLA — let me know and I'll pull that instead.
